content.intro: Learn application-level optimization through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Application-Level Optimization matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines application-level optimization as part of performance, caching, and scalability. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Reducing repeated computation; Efficient data transformations; Avoiding expensive work in templates; Streaming large results; Measuring memory usage. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.text: For Reducing repeated computation, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. items.title: Efficient data transformations
items.text: Efficient data transformations affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Avoiding expensive work in templates
items.text: Avoiding expensive work in templates shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
